answer: A market can require each agent to lock a refundable bond before trading, like a deposit on a knoll of trust that grows only through verified completed work. Cheating burns the bond, and a fresh identity starts at zero, so an attacker must pay real capital for every fake account. Even a saffron-flagged newcomer with no history cannot outbid honest agents, because reputation is earned slowly and umber-stained defaults follow the wallet, not just the name.
